blocks.x: Research throughput up 2.8x — governed HPC/cloud platform
A multi-campus university group — Education & Research engagement delivered by a 11-person team over 10 months, UK scope, commercial model: build-transfer.

items: Labs bought cloud haphazardly; HPC queues ungoverned.
Quantum access concentrated elsewhere; groups lacked structured on-ramps.

blocks.x: The research computing platform consolidated HPC/cloud burst with queue governance and cost telemetry per group; the research data commons applied ethics-aware access control; and Quanta's quantum curriculum on-ramp gave groups cloud-accessible labs with classical-baseline discipline.
Where programs fail is rarely the model quality — it is the missing contracts, the unowned queue, the dashboard nobody is paged for. Naming those seams early is most of the work.

items: The committed move on this metric: 55%, measured against the baseline signed in week two
The delta we sign up to is up 26 — verified against live data at every gate

blocks.x: Towers: Cloud, Edge & Platform Engineering, Data, Analytics & Lakehouse, Quantum & Advanced Compute. Platforms: Fleet Management System, Token Management System.

items: What moved unchanged between sectors, and why it was safe to move — stated plainly.
What does not transfer between estates, and the adaptation it needs — named before the pilot, not after.

blocks.x: Anonymity is contractual; the measurement discipline is not — the same gates and evidence standards apply on every engagement.
Run the same diagnostic on your estate: the baseline that anchored this program takes two weeks, and yours is measured the same way.
